questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'She ___ her homework right now.'
questions.context: Evening study session at a school in Santa Tecla, SV.

options.feedback: 'She' is third person singular, so it takes 'is' plus the -ing form of 'do', which gives 'is doing'.
'Do' is the plain form of the verb; it needs an auxiliary such as 'does' or the -ing ending to make the present continuous.
The -ing form cannot stand alone in this tense; it requires the verb 'to be' in front of it.
'Does' belongs to the present simple in questions and negatives, not to the present continuous.

questions.explanation: The present continuous is made with the verb 'to be' in the present form plus the -ing form of the main verb, so the sentence needs 'is doing'.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is in the present continuous?
questions.context: Comparing tense forms on the classroom board in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: The children played in the yard yesterday.
options.feedback: 'Played' is the past simple, so this sentence sits in the past, not the present continuous.

options.text: The children are playing in the yard.
options.feedback: It joins 'are' with the -ing form 'playing', which is exactly the present continuous pattern.

options.text: The children play in the yard every day.
options.feedback: 'Play' has no auxiliary and no -ing ending, so this is the present simple for habits.

options.text: The children will play in the yard tomorrow.
options.feedback: 'Will' marks the future simple, so this sentence is not in the present continuous.

questions.explanation: Only the sentence built with 'am/is/are' plus an -ing form sits in the present continuous; the other three use other tenses.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'I ___ understand this exercise.'
questions.context: A classmate asks for help during a math class in Soyapango, SV.

options.feedback: In English the auxiliary comes before 'not'; 'not am' is the wrong order and no one would say it.
'Do not' builds the negative of the present simple, not of the present continuous.
'Not' goes after 'am' and before the -ing form: 'am not understanding' completes the negative.
English builds the negative of 'be' with the word 'not', which is why we say 'am not' and never 'am no'.

questions.explanation: To make a negative in the present continuous, place 'not' between the auxiliary 'am/is/are' and the -ing form.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the question: 'What ___ you doing after class?'
questions.context: A teacher in Ahuachapan asks the class about their plans.

options.feedback: 'Is' goes with he, she and it; with 'you' the auxiliary must be 'are'.
'Do' forms the present simple in questions, so 'What do you do after class' is a different question about habits.
'Will' signals the future, so the question would ask about later plans rather than what is happening now.
'You' pairs with 'are', so the question becomes 'What are you doing', which is correct.

questions.explanation: The question word 'what' comes first and the subject 'you' requires the auxiliary 'are' before the -ing form.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct form of the verb in the present continuous: 'They ___ (watch) a documentary.'
questions.context: A film screening for a grade 11 class in San Miguel, SV.

options.feedback: English never adds an extra 'e' before -ing; 'watcheing' is not a form of any verb.
The letter 'y' is not used with -ing; the correct spelling is 'watching'.
'Watched' is the past simple, and past forms do not appear in the present continuous.
'Watch' keeps its full spelling and simply takes -ing, which gives 'watching'.

questions.explanation: To build the -ing form of 'watch' from the base verb, remove the final -ch sound and add -ing, so it becomes 'watching'.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'The baby ___ (sit) on the floor.'
questions.context: A photo description task in a language lab in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: English doubles the final consonant of 'sit' before -ing, so the single 't' spelling is wrong.
'Sits' is the present simple in third person and carries no -ing ending at all.
The final 't' doubles before -ing, and the subject 'the baby' takes 'is', giving 'is sitting'.
'The baby' is singular, so the auxiliary must be 'is' and not 'are'.

questions.explanation: When a verb ends in a single consonant after a short vowel, the final consonant doubles before -ing, so 'sit' becomes 'sitting'.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct contraction: 'She is not ___ the answer.'
questions.context: An oral exercise in a secondary school in Usulutan, SV.

options.feedback: Writing 'isnt' without an apostrophe loses the missing letter and is misspelled.
'Is not' shortens to "isn't" with an apostrophe replacing the missing 'o'.
"Aren't" contracts 'are not', which cannot be used with the singular subject 'she'.
"Doesn't" contracts 'does not' and belongs to the present simple, not to the verb 'be'.

questions.explanation: 'Is not' contracts to 'isn't' in English, so the negative sentence reads "She isn't the answer".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which time expression usually goes with the present continuous?
questions.context: A grammar summary written on the board in Apopa, SV.

options.feedback: 'At the moment' points to an action happening now, which is exactly the use of the present continuous.
'Every day' describes a repeated habit, so it goes with the present simple instead.
'Yesterday' places the action in the past, which belongs to a past tense.
'Last week' is a finished past period, so the present continuous cannot be used with it.

questions.explanation: Words such as 'now', 'at the moment' and 'look' describe an action in progress, which is the meaning of the present continuous.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'Look! It ___ (rain) again.'
questions.context: Students looking out of the window during a class in Chalatenango, SV.

options.feedback: 'Rains' is the present simple; the progress sign 'Look!' calls for the present continuous.
'Look!' signals an action in progress at this moment, so 'is raining' is the correct form.
'Rained' is the past simple and cannot follow 'Look!' in the present continuous.
'Will rain' is the future simple, and nothing in the sentence points to a future moment.

questions.explanation: 'Look!' introduces an action you can see happening right now, so the verb takes 'is' plus the -ing form 'raining'.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'I ___ (listen) to a podcast while I run.'
questions.context: A student describes his routine in a first-week interview in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: The bare verb 'listen' cannot follow 'am'; the present continuous needs the -ing form.
'Listen' must be followed by 'to' before its object, so 'listening' alone is incomplete.
'Listens' is the present simple in third person, which does not match the subject 'I'.
'Listen to' keeps the preposition 'to' after the -ing form, so the answer is 'am listening to'.

questions.explanation: The verb 'listen' is followed by 'to' plus its object, and in the present continuous the -ing form keeps that pattern: 'listening to'.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which pair of verbs both need the -ing form?
questions.context: A spelling drill in a school in Santa Tecla, SV.

options.feedback: 'Need' gives 'needing' and 'prefer' gives 'preferring', and the second one doubles the final r.
'Begin' and 'open' both take -ing unchanged, so this pair is also regular.
'Write' gives 'writing' and 'dance' gives 'dancing'; neither verb doubles a letter before -ing.
'Listen' gives 'listening' and 'visit' gives 'visiting', both without any change.

questions.explanation: Both 'write' and 'dance' form the present continuous with -ing, and both keep their spelling with no extra consonant to double.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'Where ___ your parents living now?'
questions.context: A visitor asks a host family in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'Are' agrees with the plural 'parents' and builds the present continuous with 'living'.
'Is' goes with singular subjects such as 'he', 'she' or 'the parent'.
'Do' builds the present simple, which would give a question about a permanent address.
'Were' is the past auxiliary and cannot describe a situation that holds right now.

questions.explanation: 'Now' requires the present continuous, and the plural subject 'your parents' takes the auxiliary 'are' before the -ing form.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'We ___ (not / use) the gym because it is closed.'
questions.context: A message left on the school notice board in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: The auxiliary comes before 'not' in English, so 'not are' is the wrong word order.
'Do not use' is the negative of the present simple and lacks the -ing form.
After 'are not' the verb must take its -ing form, so the bare 'use' cannot follow.
'Are not using' is the present continuous negative: 'are' for 'we' and 'not' before 'using'.

questions.explanation: The subject 'we' takes 'are' in the present continuous, and the negative places 'not' between the auxiliary and the -ing form.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct -ing form: 'She enjoys ___ (swim) in the ocean.'
questions.context: A conversation about hobbies in a summer school in La Libertad, SV.

options.feedback: 'Swiming' keeps the final e, which English drops before -ing, so the spelling is wrong.
'Enjoy' is followed by a gerund, and 'swim' becomes 'swimming' when it adds -ing.
'Enjoy' does not take an infinitive; it requires the -ing form of the following verb.
'Swam' is the past simple of 'swim' and cannot follow 'enjoys'.

questions.explanation: After the verb 'enjoy' the -ing form of the next verb is required, and 'swim' drops its silent e before taking -ing.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'The teacher ___ (explain) the grammar now.'
questions.context: A live lesson at a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'The teacher' is third person singular, so 'is' plus 'explaining' is correct.
'Are' goes with plural or second person subjects, not with 'the teacher'.
'Explain' has no auxiliary and no -ing ending, so it is the present simple.
'Was explaining' is the past continuous and cannot describe a lesson happening now.

questions.explanation: With the third person singular subject 'the teacher' the auxiliary is 'is', so the present continuous is 'is explaining'.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence describes an action that is finished?
questions.context: A question about the tense of a sentence in a grammar test in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: I am finishing my homework right now.
options.feedback: 'Am finishing' describes an action still in progress at this moment.

options.text: I am finishing my homework at the moment.
options.feedback: 'At the moment' places the action in progress, which is the present continuous.

options.text: I finish my homework every afternoon.
options.feedback: 'Finish' with the frequency expression 'every afternoon' describes a repeated habit.

options.text: I am finishing my homework tonight.
options.feedback: 'Tonight' with the present continuous places the action around now, so it is not finished.

questions.explanation: The present continuous describes an action in progress, so the sentence describing a finished action must use the present simple.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'They ___ (play) chess right now.'
questions.context: A break-time scene in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'Is' goes with singular subjects, so it does not agree with the plural 'they'.
'They' takes 'are' and 'play' simply takes -ing, so 'are playing' is correct.
'Plays' is the present simple in third person and has no -ing ending.
After 'are' the verb must take its -ing form, so the bare 'play' cannot follow.

questions.explanation: 'Play' keeps its spelling and adds -ing, and the plural subject 'they' requires 'are', giving 'are playing'.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct question: '___ your sister studying for the exam?'
questions.context: An evening phone call recorded for a listening activity in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'Is' opens the question and agrees with the singular subject 'your sister'.
'Are' would require a plural subject, but 'your sister' is singular.
'Does' forms the present simple question and would need the base verb 'study'.
'Did' is the past auxiliary and would describe an action that has already finished.

questions.explanation: In a present continuous question the auxiliary 'is' comes first, before the subject 'your sister' and the -ing form.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'The baby ___ (cry) because she is hungry.'
questions.context: A picture description in a language class in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'Cries' is the present simple, which presents the crying as a repeated habit.
'Was crying' is the past continuous and would need a past reference point in the sentence.
The situation is happening at the moment of speaking, so 'is crying' is the natural choice.
'Will cry' is the future simple and does not match a situation described as already underway.

questions.explanation: 'Because' introduces a reason for an action happening right now, so 'is crying' fits the situation described.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct option: 'It ___ (snow) in the mountains this morning.'
questions.context: A weather report read aloud in a language class in San Salvador, SV.

options.feedback: 'It' is singular, so the auxiliary must be 'is' and never 'are'.
'Snow' alone has no auxiliary, which would make the sentence the present simple.
After the auxiliary 'is' the verb must take its -ing form, so the bare 'snow' cannot follow.
'It' takes 'is' and 'snow' keeps its spelling before -ing, giving 'is snowing'.

questions.explanation: 'It' is the third person singular subject used with the weather, so the auxiliary is 'is' and the verb 'snow' simply takes -ing.
questions.subject: ingles
